test_title: PYST 18: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following officials toured Mauryan provinces every five years to inspect administration and submit reports on provincial governance?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Pradeshika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradeshika** was a provincial officer during the **Mauryan period**.
 
• They were responsible for touring the provinces every five years to inspect the **administration**.
 
• Their duties included submitting reports on the **provincial governance** to the central authority.
 
• The inspection ensured that the **policies of the central government** were implemented effectively at the provincial level.
 
• This role was significant in maintaining the efficiency and control of the **Mauryan Empire**, which was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, and the **Pradeshika** played a crucial role in the functioning of this system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rajuka**__

 __
 
• The **Rajuka** was another official during the Mauryan period, primarily responsible for **judicial and administrative duties** in the provinces.
 
• They were tasked with overseeing issues related to **land revenue and justice**.
 
• They did not tour the provinces regularly like the **Pradeshika**.
 
 
 
• **Nagarika**__
 __
 
• The **Nagarika** was an officer responsible for the **urban administration**.
 
• They managed the affairs of cities and towns, ensuring smooth functioning of daily life and **law and order**.
 
• Unlike the **Pradeshika**, they worked in urban areas and did not inspect provinces.
 
 
 
• **Amatya**__
 
 
• The **Amatya** was a minister or high-ranking official in the Mauryan administration.
 
• They were involved in the **formulation of policies** and advising the king on administrative matters.
 
• They did not have the specific duty of touring provinces to inspect administration like the **Pradeshika**.
